title: Draw the Arrow

source.quote: the opening communication is called the stimulus. The reply is called the response.

setting: Wednesday, 10:05am - before the Friday release goes sideways, back when this is just a normal check-in. Arjun is mid-deploy, headphones on.

L1.line: Hey - did the hotfix actually go out last night?
L1.question: Priya's line lands on Arjun's desk. Which ego state is it coming from, and has a transaction actually happened yet?

options.text: Parent - she's checking up on him, which is a Parent move.
options.feedback: The content (checking on someone's work) could sound Parental, but the cues - even tone, plain question, no judgment - don't fit Parent. Diagnose from cues, not content.

options.text: Adult - a plain request for current information. And no: this is only the stimulus so far, not a transaction yet.
options.feedback: Right. Flat, factual, present-tense is Adult. And by definition a transaction needs a stimulus AND a response - right now there's only a stimulus on the table.

options.text: Child - she sounds anxious about it underneath.
options.feedback: There's no cue for anxious Child here - no hedging, no rising pitch, no apology. Just a clean request for data.

L1.lesson: A transaction is a stimulus plus a response - Berne's "basic unit of social discourse." One line, however clearly it comes from an ego state, is only ever half of one.

L2.intro: Arjun looks up and answers. Watch where the vectors land before you reply.

beats.line: Yeah, it went out around 11. I ran the smoke tests myself before I called it done.

options.text: Good - can you paste the test output in the channel so Deepa can sign off?
options.outcome: "Sure, give me a sec." He pastes it without missing a beat. The exchange stays easy, specific, moving.
options.lesson: A complementary transaction is one where the vectors are parallel and the ego-state addressed is the one that answers - Adult asked, Adult answered, so by rule 1 (answer the exact state you were addressed in, and the exchange can just keep going) this one simply continues.

options.text: Thank you so much for staying on top of this, you're amazing.
options.outcome: "Oh - thanks." He looks pleased but a little unsure what to do with it; the actual question about test output still hasn't been asked.
options.lesson: Nurturing Parent to his Free Child is warm and still complementary - it just isn't the same transaction as confirming the work, and the follow-up still needs asking for.

options.text: Are you sure it's actually fine? I don't love finding this out after the fact.
options.outcome: His face shuts. "I said I tested it." The easy exchange is gone; now you're both defending positions instead of looking at test output.
options.lesson: Crossing is a legitimate tool (rule 2: answer from a different state than the one addressed, and the exchange breaks until someone shifts) but it isn't free - crossing an Adult report with a Child's doubt, when nothing has actually gone wrong yet, manufactures a fight that wasn't there a line ago.

fields.label: Draw the vectors for this exchange, and for a version where Arjun answered defensively instead.

pairs.label: If Arjun had answered like a scolded kid instead

fields.label: In under 50 words: why isn't Priya's opening line, on its own, a transaction? What has to happen for it to become one?

echo.setting: Six hours later, a Slack DM from a different teammate.
echo.line: quick q - is the staging env up right now?
